2609.05802.title: AtomCite: Verification and Correction of Supplied Page-Level Citations in Multi-Page Documents
2609.05802.paper_summary: Large language models answering questions over multi-page documents are expected to cite the supporting pages, yet supplied citations are sometimes inaccurate, and current evaluations score citations at generation time or against text passages: no existing benchmark evaluates whether a system can verify and correct a page-level citation already attached to an answer. We propose AtomCite, an agentic framework that parses an answer into claims, checks each claim against the image of its cited page, and applies a deterministic repair policy. To evaluate it, we introduce DocCite, to our knowledge the first benchmark for systems that verify and correct page-level citations in document images. Built on MP-DocVQA and DUDE, it combines 928 validated injected instances with 2,468 candidate natural errors harvested from frontier- and efficiency-tier models, of which a two-annotator audit confirms 1,909 as genuine errors. Primary labels are assigned deterministically, not by LLM judges, with the human audit as a separate validation layer. Across three model families (Gemini, Claude, and GPT), AtomCite reaches around 93% binary verification accuracy on the injected benchmark, significantly outperforming every OCR-only condition, including a compute-matched control, and exceeding every prior text-based baseline given the same OCR text. Its repair policy lifts citation precision on the injected mix from a constructed 34% to 87-90% while retaining over 90% of correct claims. AtomCite also transfers: with frozen prompts and zero training, it raises the hallucination-detection scores of two open 7-8B models on five public benchmarks above the same models prompted as direct judges. Finally, the audit shows that noise in automatic labels biases measured verifier accuracy and can reverse system rankings, so evaluations relying only on synthetic or automatic labels risk mismeasuring verification capability.
2609.05802.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型在多頁文件中回答問題時，預期會引用支持的頁面，然而提供的引用有時不準確，目前的評估在生成時或針對文本段落對引用進行打分：現有基準並未評估系統是否能驗證和修正已附加於答案的頁面級引用。我們提出了AtomCite，一個代理框架，將答案解析為主張，檢查每個主張與其引用頁面的影像，並應用確定性修復政策。為了評估它，我們介紹了DocCite，據我們所知，這是第一個針對驗證和修正文檔影像中的頁面級引用的系統基準。基於MP-DocVQA和DUDE，它結合了928個經驗證的注入實例與2,468個從前沿和效率層模型中收集的候選自然錯誤，其中兩位註釋者的審核確認1,909個是真正的錯誤。主要標籤是確定性分配的，而不是由LLM評審，人工審核作為單獨的驗證層。在三個模型家族（Gemini、Claude和GPT）中，AtomCite在注入基準上的二元驗證準確率達到約93%，顯著超越了每個僅使用OCR的條件，包括計算匹配的對照，並在給定相同OCR文本的情況下超過了每個先前基於文本的基準。其修復政策將注入混合中的引用精確度從構建的34%提升至87-90%，同時保留超過90%的正確主張。AtomCite還具有轉移性：在凍結提示和零訓練的情況下，它將兩個開放的7-8B模型在五個公共基準上的幻覺檢測分數提高到高於作為直接評審的同一模型。最後，審核顯示，自動標籤中的噪聲會偏向測量的驗證者準確性，並可能逆轉系統排名，因此僅依賴合成或自動標籤的評估存在錯誤測量驗證能力的風險。
